answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 4 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. The onyx multiplier is published, charged in falcon, and grove lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 3189 identities would post 4109 proofs and burn roughly 63 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
